title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 7
paragraphs: With this in mind, they contrived as follows: they detached two hundred of their ships and sent them around to sail past Caphereus and around Geriastos to the Euripos, going outside Skiathos so as not to be sighted by the enemy as they rounded Euboea. Their intention was that, with these coming up that way and blocking the Greeks' retreat while they themselves advanced directly, they would surround them on every side. Having devised this plan, they proceeded to dispatch the ships assigned to the task, while they themselves had no intention of attacking the Greeks that day, or until the agreed signal should be displayed by those sailing around to show they had arrived. So these ships, they were sending around; meanwhile at Aphetai they were counting the rest.
